metadata.title: How to remove tiles
metadata.description: Removing tiles can be tricky, it is best to take a methodical approach rather than going at it like a bull in a china shop. Here we remove wall tiles using a knock through screwdriver and hammer. Brought to you by http://www.ultimatehandyman.co.uk/forum1/

nodes.plm_caption:
A person is removing old tiles from a wall and then replacing them. A wall can be seen in the background and a tile with glue on its surface. A hammer and screw driver are visible. A song is playing in the background. The person is wearing a white T-shirt and protective gloves.
The person initially removes one tile by placing its edge against the wall and pushing it away from themself with a hammer. Then they point the screwdriver against the tile and hit it a few times before turning it and removing the tile. The next action done is the same as above. Finally the person points to the hole in the wall and tries to fill it. The person then taps on the wall and removes two stones from the wall and touches another tile.
The floor and the bottom of the wall are visible.

summary.brief: A person in a white T‑shirt and gloves removes bathroom tiles with a screwdriver and hammer, then peels away damaged plaster and loose stones from the exposed wall before the video ends with a handyman advertisement.
summary.detailed: The video opens with a title screen that reads “How to remove tiles.” It then cuts to a bathroom where a white bathtub, a yellow‑green bucket and a blue trash bag are visible. A person wearing a white T‑shirt, safety glasses and gloves holds a large flat‑head screwdriver in the left hand and a claw hammer in the right. He places the screwdriver against the edge of each tile, taps it with the hammer to loosen the tile, twists the screwdriver to pry the tile free and drops the tile into the bucket. This process is repeated until a section of wall is cleared of tiles. The camera then focuses on the exposed wall, which shows extensive plaster damage: cracked, flaking plaster and sections of plasterboard that are detached from the brick behind it. The person points to the damaged areas, runs his hand over them and manually peels away loose plaster and a few protruding stone pieces, exposing the underlying brick core. The hand continues to lift off pieces of concrete from the wall. The segment concludes with a title screen and a static advertisement for Ultimate Handyman featuring a hammer and circular‑saw logo.

action.detailed: Use a screwdriver and a claw hammer to pry each tile from the wall, then use your hand to peel away the loose plaster and stones from the exposed surface.
action.actor: A person wearing a white T‑shirt, safety glasses, and gloves

nodes.plm_caption:
A person is in the process of removing tiles from a wall. The video starts with a tutorial page with the words "How to remove tiles" in white letters with a graphic on the page. At the end, the tutorial page has disappeared, and there's a white bathtub inside a room. A green yellow plastic container with a blue plastic bag that has black trash inside of it. The man shows the tub's silver faucet by turning it clockwise and counterclockwise.
The man is holding a screw driver in his left hand, then places it against the wall. He hits the driver with a claw hammer in his right hand to remove the tile. At some point, he removes some of the tile and keeps removing tile until all of the tiles have been removed. At the end, he moves away from the wall.

summary.brief: A man removes wall tiles using a screwdriver and hammer while wearing safety gear.
summary.detailed: The video opens with a black title card that reads “How to remove tiles” and shows the Ultimate Handyman logo. It then cuts to a bathroom where a white bathtub, a green‑yellow bucket and a blue trash bag are visible. A man wearing safety glasses, gloves and a white T‑shirt briefly turns the bathtub’s silver faucet clockwise and counter‑clockwise. He picks up a knock‑through screwdriver in his left hand, presses the tip against the edge of a tile, and repeatedly strikes the screwdriver with a claw hammer in his right hand to pry the tile loose. Each loosened tile is set aside in the bucket or on the floor. He repeats this method across the entire wall, systematically removing every tile until the wall is completely bare, and then steps back from the wall as the title screen fades.

action.detailed: Hold the screwdriver against a tile with the left hand, strike it repeatedly with the claw hammer in the right hand to loosen the tile, pull the tile away, and continue this procedure across the wall until all tiles are removed, then step back from the wall.
action.actor: A man wearing safety glasses, gloves and a white T‑shirt

nodes.plm_caption: A man is peeling a wall. The wall is deteriorating and old.

summary.brief: A hand peels away flaking plaster and concrete from a damaged wall, revealing the brick behind.
summary.detailed: The segment begins with a close‑up of a gray‑brown wall that shows cracked, layered plaster and peeling paint. The presenter points with the left hand and pulls off loose white and gray plaster, then lifts pieces of concrete, moving from the lower part of the wall upward. As the flaky material is removed, the underlying red brick becomes visible. The hand continues to strip larger patches until the wall is largely cleared, after which the video cuts to an end‑card advertising Ultimate Handyman.

action.detailed: Pull off the flaking plaster and concrete from the wall with your hand, working upward to expose the brick underneath.
action.actor: The presenter’s hand (the only visible part of the person demonstrating the repair)

nodes.plm_caption:
A man wearing safety equipment demonstrates how to install tile. The tiles are white, and the adhesive is a color cream. There are multiple tiles in the background that have been installed for years and a few that have been partially installed, he is demonstrating how to do it. In the beginning, he is explaining the process while another individual uses a machine to create the space needed to lay the tile adhesives, before the man with safety gear begins the installation.
The machine in the background makes the small spaces in the tiles where the adhesives need to be inserted, while the other man with the bucket creates the adhesive that he puts on the spaces made in the tiles.
The space the man with safety gear uses to lay tile. The man makes multiple holes in the wall. When one tile is laid, the space from his previous hole is filled and the other hole is filled with adhesive to lay another tile.

summary.brief: A man in safety gear removes old wall tiles and installs new white tiles using a hammer, screwdriver and mortar.
summary.detailed: The video opens with a title card and then shows a bathroom wall covered with white tiles. A man wearing a white T‑shirt, grey gloves and safety glasses picks up a blue bag in a green bucket placed in the bathtub and then grabs a large knock‑through screwdriver and a claw hammer. He strikes the screwdriver with the hammer to pry the existing tiles loose, dropping the broken pieces into the bucket. After clearing a section of the wall, he spreads a cream‑coloured mortar onto the exposed surface, lines up new white tiles, and taps each tile into the mortar with a hammer and a small metal tool while checking alignment with a level. He repeats the process across the wall, smoothing excess mortar as needed, and finishes by stepping back from the completed area.

action.detailed: Prise off the old tiles with a hammer and screwdriver, then spread mortar on the wall and tap new tiles into place with a hammer and metal tool while using a level to align them.
action.actor: a man wearing a white T‑shirt, grey gloves and safety glasses

nodes.plm_caption: This video shows walls with peeling paint and wallpaper. The walls look old and in need of repair.

summary.brief: The segment shows a rundown bathroom with peeling wallpaper and paint, an exposed white bathtub, and a voice‑over describing the wall’s renovation progress.
summary.detailed: The video opens on a dimly lit bathroom wall where paint and grey wallpaper are flaking, revealing a brown‑gray substrate underneath. Light briefly brightens, exposing a white bathtub placed in a corner, a vertical wooden board or beam behind it, and metal pipes with a tap. The camera pans left and right, showing uneven, rough drywall texture, sections where wallpaper has been removed, and patches of paint in blue, green, brown and gray that have peeled away. A wooden board with red pipes runs across a doorway, and a water spigot with a blue fixture is visible above it. The view then shifts to close‑ups of raw cement and exposed plaster where the old surface has been stripped, showing grey concrete and spots of mud or adhesive. A voice‑over begins, stating that the next wall is almost finished, and the camera moves to a close‑up of that wall, then to the opposite side, noting it is a little more finished. Further camera movement shows a grey, peeling wall with exposed wood beams at the base of a shower, a white faucet and reflections on the metal. The segment ends with close‑up shots of a wall where plaster has been removed, new paper covering the top, and uneven white paint strokes on rough concrete before fading to black.

A person's hand touches a large patch of a peeling wall. Two subsequent times, the hand peels a piece of concrete from that spot in the wall. The video ends with the title screen.
The hand can only be seen from the wrist up in some shots; the hand is the only part of the human body in any shot.
The background is a wall composed of a red brick core with a layer of plaster over it. The other areas of the wall are covered in plaster and paper, and one of the pipes has paper partially covering it. In one shot, two grey planks are visible on the wall between the peeling area and another part of the wall. In another shot, the bottom of the wall is white, with the floor below it barely visible. In the last shot, the black background shows a circular saw with a red and silver blade and a hammer with a black handle and yellow accent.
The video ends with an ad for the Ultimate Handyman. In the ad, the text reads "Thanks for watching" (top), an image of a hammer and circular saw in the center, a logo for "Ultimate Handyman" in red and blue text over the top of the image, a line of white text that reads "www.ultimatelyhandyman.co.uk", and a line of smaller white text that reads " come and join us @".

summary.brief: A hand peels away loose wall material to expose the brick behind, and the segment ends with the Ultimate Handyman outro screen.
summary.detailed: The segment opens with a close‑up of a wrist‑up hand touching a large, peeling area on a wall whose core is red brick covered by plaster and paper. The hand grips the loose plaster‑like (cement) layer and pulls it away, removing a piece of material. The camera then shows the hand pointing to two scored lines on the peeled surface, inserting a finger into a rectangular hole and peeling another fragment off. The view widens to reveal the worker’s forearms and upper body (blue jeans and a grey‑blue logo T‑shirt) as they continue to strip additional chunks from the lower part of the wall, moving upward past two grey metal planks, a pipe partially wrapped in paper, and a white‑finished base. As the deteriorated material is removed, the underlying red brick becomes visible. The final moments switch to a black end‑card that displays “Thanks for watching” together with the Ultimate Handyman logo, a hammer and circular saw, and the website address.

action.detailed: Grip the loose plaster or cement with the hand and pull it away from the wall, then repeat the motion to strip additional sections and reveal the brick underneath.
action.actor: A person's hand and forearm (visible from the wrist upward, wearing blue jeans and a grey‑blue logo T‑shirt)

A man in a bathroom is getting a bag to remove a tile. The bag is blue and it is placed in a green bucket in the bathtub. The tile is white and has some brownish marks as well.
The man is not making much effort to remove the tile, he just takes a hammer and a pry tool and starts to get ready to pull the tile up.
There is also another man who appears from the right and is looking at the bag as well.

summary.brief: In a bathroom a blue bag in a green bucket is shown before a man in a white shirt lifts a hammer‑like tool to ready a white tile for removal, while another man arrives holding a claw hammer and a metal rod.
summary.detailed: The video begins with a black title card that reads “How to remove tiles.” It then cuts to a dimly lit bathroom where a yellow‑green bucket containing a blue plastic bag sits in a white bathtub. A hand wearing a gray work glove lifts the bucket and the bag, then reaches for a hammer‑shaped pry tool, moving the tool up and down and toward the left side of the frame. The camera shows a tiled wall with several missing tiles, including a white tile that has brownish marks. A man wearing a white T‑shirt and white gloves steps into view, holds the pry tool against the wall, shakes it, raises it, and appears ready to pry the tile loose. Shortly after, a second man enters from the right, also gloved, carrying a claw hammer in one hand and a long metal rod in the other; he shakes the hammer, lifts it, drops it onto the floor, and then holds the rod. The segment ends with the first man still holding the tool, poised to remove the tile.

action.detailed: Raise a hammer‑style pry tool, tap it against the wall and position it to pry the white tile away.
action.actor: The man wearing a white T‑shirt and white gloves

nodes.plm_caption:
This video features a man placing and hammering tiles against the wall while describing his method. He wears a white t-shirt, grey gloves, and black safety glasses while standing indoors in front of a wall with greyish light-colored tiles that already exist. He uses tools, one with a red rubber handle and the other with a black handle, to lay two tiles in a corner in a horizontal direction. 
The lighting is bright, there is a ceiling visible in the video, and the floor is not visible. The tiles make a line where they are placed horizontally, and the other tiles make another line vertically. The wall has pastel blue behind the tiles, and there is a wooden piece at the very top. The man is an experienced professional who is well prepared for the task. There is a brief dark cut out in the video.

summary.brief: A man removes damaged wall tiles and installs new ones using a hammer, screwdriver and other tools while wearing safety gear.
summary.detailed: Wearing a white T‑shirt, grey gloves and safety glasses, the man works in front of a light‑coloured tiled wall with a pastel‑blue area behind it and a wooden strip at the top. He first strikes a screwdriver with a hammer to drive the tip behind cracked tiles, prying each tile loose and dropping the broken pieces into a bucket. He sometimes uses a chisel to keep the screwdriver flat against the wall. After a section is cleared, he spreads mortar, slides a fresh tile into position, and taps it firmly with a small hammer to set it. He checks the alignment with a level or straight edge, then repeats the removal‑and‑replacement cycle across the corner and along the wall. Bright overhead lighting remains throughout, with occasional quick cuts and a brief dark transition.

action.detailed: Strike the screwdriver with the hammer to loosen each damaged tile, pull the tile away, discard it, apply mortar to the cleared area, fit a new tile, tap it into place with the hammer, align it with a level, and repeat the process across the wall.
action.actor: A man in a white T‑shirt, grey gloves and safety glasses

This video shows a person removing a layer of cement from a wall. The layer of cement is being removed to reveal more of the brickwork beneath.

This video is of a hand with a gray glove holding a yellow-green bucket with a blue plastic bag in it in a bathtub. It pans to a tiled wall, and a person is partially in frame. They reach and grab a tool with a hammer like handle.
There are three tiles missing along the top of the wall, and there is blue plastic hanging from the bucket on the far side of the tub. The hand lifts the black bag and slightly removes the bucket from the tub. The hand then holds the tool with a hammer type handle up to the camera. The hand pulls the tool downwards towards the bucket and lifts it back to the camera and down a third time to the left.
The hand is in a gray work glove and the arm wears a white shirt sleeve. This is a small section of wall that is missing paint, tiles, or adhesive.
The wall has a diagonal sunken pattern going up in the left corner. On the right is a shiny pattern of brown tiles. The hand wearing a white sleeve reaches into frame, holding a tool of some sort. The right hand lifts the tool and holds it in frame with the left. They then move the left hand down and lift the tool again to the camera. They place it at the bottom of frame. They pull the tool up to the left once more to frame and then down to the bottom, moving left to frame once more, and then up to the top again.

summary.brief: A gloved hand lifts a bucket and moves a hammer‑shaped tool, then a man in a white T‑shirt demonstrates hammer and screwdriver motions in front of a tiled wall.
summary.detailed: The segment begins with a close‑up of a white bathtub. A hand wearing a gray work glove lifts a yellow‑green bucket that contains a blue plastic bag, pulling the bucket slightly out of the tub. The same hand grabs a tool with a hammer‑shaped handle, raises it toward the camera, pulls it down toward the bucket, lifts it again, and repeats the motion moving left while the camera shows a tiled wall with three missing tiles at the top, a diagonal sunken pattern in the left corner and shiny brown tiles on the right. Next, a man wearing a white T‑shirt and white gloves steps into the frame from the left. He holds a claw hammer in his right hand and a long metal rod (a knock‑through screwdriver) in his left. He shakes the hammer back and forth a few times, raises it above his head, shakes it again, and then drops the hammer onto the floor. He then picks up the hammer with his left hand.

summary_sent_to_llm.description: Removing tiles can be tricky, it is best to take a methodical approach rather than going at it like a bull in a china shop. Here we remove wall tiles using a knock through screwdriver and hammer. Brought to you by http://www.ultimatehandyman.co.uk/forum1/
summary_sent_to_llm.root_summary: The video opens with a title screen that reads “How to remove tiles.” It then cuts to a bathroom where a white bathtub, a yellow‑green bucket and a blue trash bag are visible. A person wearing a white T‑shirt, safety glasses and gloves holds a large flat‑head screwdriver in the left hand and a claw hammer in the right. He places the screwdriver against the edge of each tile, taps it with the hammer to loosen the tile, twists the screwdriver to pry the tile free and drops the tile into the bucket. This process is repeated until a section of wall is cleared of tiles. The camera then focuses on the exposed wall, which shows extensive plaster damage: cracked, flaking plaster and sections of plasterboard that are detached from the brick behind it. The person points to the damaged areas, runs his hand over them and manually peels away loose plaster and a few protruding stone pieces, exposing the underlying brick core. The hand continues to lift off pieces of concrete from the wall. The segment concludes with a title screen and a static advertisement for Ultimate Handyman featuring a hammer and circular‑saw logo.

You evaluate YouTube videos for a video-understanding benchmark.

You will be given an Action100M-style summary of one video: title, description,

Your job is to judge:

   - "manipulation": a person performing hand-object manipulation tasks
     with clear physical goals: assembly/disassembly, repair, crafting,
     tool use, packing, sorting. The video must show clear procedural
     manipulation, NOT just incidental hand movement (e.g. a vlog where
     someone holds things while talking does NOT count).
   - "navigation": the camera moves through a physical environment as an
     agent traverses space — first-person walking tours (museum, store,
     home, city street), driving / cycling / hiking POV footage, drone
     fly-throughs of indoor or outdoor scenes, room/house walkthroughs.
     The camera's translation through the environment IS the main content.
     Does NOT count: a stationary tripod with someone talking; a tutorial
     filmed in one place; b-roll where the camera only pans or zooms but
